title: Why Does Cathay Make Finding Awards so Difficult?
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Cathay Pacific’s new “Aria Suites” Business Class. Photo: Cathay Pacific.
Airlines are certainly making it harder to secure reward seats. From Singapore Airlines deliberately preventing KrisFlyer members with low mileage balances from searching for award seats online , to Qatar Airways quietly restricting award bookings from family and friends . It appears that Cathay Pacific is joining the club by making it less straightforward to find those highly desirable seats.
Cathay Pacific has slightly changed how availability is displayed
Cathay has subtly altered the visibility of award availability on its website. Previously, the interface clearly indicated whether seats were available or not by displaying either “Not available” or the number of Asia Miles required.
Previous display of award availability on the Cathay Pacific website.
Currently, if you search a date with no availability, the site still shows a clear “no availability” message.
No award availability message on Cathay Pacific website
But once you move to dates that do have seats, the experience becomes less intuitive.
For example, Saturday 10 July 2027 shows availability, yet the number of Asia Miles required is not displayed. Adjacent dates also lack any clear indication of whether seats are available, forcing you to click through each one individually.
Cathay Pacific availability unclearly displayed
You will need to search alltogether to see “no availability” markers, but even then, the mileage cost remains hidden.
Cathay Pacific showing award availability without the number of miles required.
This is a small change, but ultimately provides a poorer user experience, and it makes finding reward seats more time‑consuming.
Cathay Pacific is not releasing seats predictably as before
Cathay Pacific used to have great award availability , often opening multiple business class seats exactly 360 days before departure. That pattern is no longer the case.
Currently, the release timing for Cathay Pacific operated flights to Europe looks more like:
Australia to Frankfurt: ~325 days before departure.
Australia to London: ~320 days before departure.
Australia to Amsterdam: ~325 days before departure.
Australia to Milan: ~324 days before departure.
Australia to Paris: ~324 days before departure.
Australia to Barcelona: ~317 days before departure.
There is some availability to Europe via Colombo at 337 days before departure.
This is a good reminder that award availability patterns have changed and it’s key to remain flexible to secure your seats.
Finding availability through seats.aero
If you have a seats.aero Pro account, there is a new feature that allows you to search Cathay Pacific reward seats more efficiently.
You can filter by region or a specific airport, which makes it easier to spot availability.
Cathay Pacific Award Finder through seats.aero
The only catch with this tool is that you can only search flights within 180 days of departure. You can also set an alert for a Cathay Award seat as long as it’s within the 180-day window.
AFF Gold and Platinum members receive a 10% and 25% off respectively, for a new seats.aero membership.
Is Cathay making it too difficult to find already-scarce award seats? Or does this actually benefit frequent flyers who know what they’re doing? Let us know your thoughts on the AFF forum!
